text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys Scientific Explorer Bee-Ology Science Kids Science Experiment Kit This is an interesting kit, that in all fairness should probably be about a 3.5 star product, but Amazon forces me to choose, so I'll rank this on the lower end.

There is a lot to like here - the activities are pretty good, the variety is great, and the educational value is fantastic. My daughter's favorite were the bee goggles, which was the simplest activity, while I liked the idea of building the model to identify the parts of the bee. There are some simple chits that you can move around to organize a hive that look like they belong in a board game, but didn't provide a lot of interest for daughter.

There are plenty of opportunities as well. The book that comes with the set is a big miss. There is a ton of information inside that helped me answer some questions for my daughter, but it is dry as a bone, and holds no interest for her whatsoever. It's essentially an encyclopedia entry about bees, and educationally, it's fabulous, but from a kid's point of view, they forgot to include anything fun.

There is one activity that requires you have a live flower, so that will be a miss for anyone doing this kit over a fall or winter season unless they want to take a separate trip to the store.

As I said above, there were 5 activities, and while I liked one or two, there's not too much to some of them. Pollinate a flower? OK, that's done in a few minutes. Bee wings buzzing? A fun toy, not too much really make use of here. The goggles were a hit with the kid, but are a dress up accessory at best for me. The model was great. The peel and stick bit was a good idea that didn't resonate with my little one.

Overall, it's a good idea, especially given the season we've tried it in, and in combination with our outdoor bee sanctuaries and veggie garden. Giving kids an education about these pollinators is important and could be a fantastic idea for the future, but for this kit, I think there's room for improvement.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys Scientific Explorer Bee-Ology Science Kids Science Experiment Kit

Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+ We'd already bought the Sneaky Squirrel Game, which is similar to this game. We've though it was one of the cutest games ever, so we were thrilled to add this one to our collection, too!

With this game, you'll get one of the cutest boxes you've ever seen! (Let me note here that the top and bottom of the game box do NOT fit inside each other. It's the same with the squirrel game.) You'll also get a super cute pair of Shelby tweezers, 4 bowls, a packet of bones, and a double spinner.

Playing the game is pretty simple. There can be up to 4 players at a time. Each player will spin first to see if they will get bones or lose bones or just lose a turn. The second spin is to determine how many bones they will win/lose. If they land on a seagull, it means they will lose bones. If they land on the hungry pug, they get to steal bones from another player. Busy pug means they lose a turn, and landing on the bones mean they win bones for their bowl. They can pick up the bones they win/lose with the tweezers.

The tweezers are a great way to develop motor skills. The game itself is a great, fun way to learn counting skills. My 5 year old is delayed and really struggles with numbers, so I'm always thrilled to find a new, exciting way to teach them to him. This is also a fun game for my 2 year old. It IS pretty simple, so I imagine, on average, 2-4, maybe 5, is probably the best ages for this game.

Overall, this is a super cute game! I can highly recommend this AND the Sneaky Squirrel Game for your young little ones!
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+

Sew Mini Gardens (Klutz Craft Kit) The Klutz kits are hit and miss for us, but this one was a hit. Now, that said, like a lot of the Klutz kits, this is a difficult one for children, and will require a very hands on adult helper.

The designs are very nice, and the instructions are good throughout if you have Google or sewing knowledge. It's not that it's going to be terribly difficult to figure out how to sew necessarily, but some of the designs are reasonably complex. I'm not a sewer, but I could figure it out, and instruct my little ones. There are a lot of steps to some of them, and the dexterity needed means that this is going to be one for the older children almost exclusively - they'll need some "advanced" skills like maintaining an even stitch pattern that is not too widely spaced or narrow, figuring out what "whip-stitching" is without it being explained thoroughly, and so forth. Because the designs are all fairly small, you can make one, then save the rest for later, and the kit will see use for many crafting sessions.

I'm very impressed by the finished product as well. Overall, a fun and educational experience for the little ones and for myself as well.
text_fidelity_b: Sew Mini Gardens (Klutz Craft Kit)

text_fidelity_a:
SYMA X1 4 Channel 2.4G RC Quad Copter, Spacecraft (As Shown) So, this is the second one of these that I've ordered; the first was for my nephew. After flying it a bit with him, I decided to give it a try on my own. This is probably the best quadcopter value out there, though I do say this based on other reviews and not my own experience with multiple makes and models. For about $40, you get a very capable quad-copter that you can fly left/right, forward/reverse, up/down, as well as rotate it 360 to keep the "front" of the copter oriented properly, so you're not pushing the controller left and having the unit bank right. It also has a "eversion" mode that basically flips the copter 360 degrees in a loop automatically. This function works left/right and forward/backward, and is very cool,primarily because it's so easy to execute the maneuver.

The unit has a Low and High setting, which trims the controls a bit on the Low setting, and makes for a very good indoor mode while the High setting is best for outdoors and stunt moves. There are trim controls for the throttle, rotation, left/right and forward/back. I've found that the trim does work, and is best adjusted when the copter is outside and has some height off the ground...essentially, you try to hover it and see how best to adjust the controls. Ideally, if you let off the controls, the unit should hover fairly well. The system has no "auto" hover mode that'll auto-adjust the trims to hover, so getting it dialed in is still a manual affair. The controls work well, and I've flown this for maybe an hours indoors and 30 minutes outside, and feel as if I have good control of the thing.

I've found this to be a very sturdy unit, having crashed it numerous times in just about every orientation. It does come with a set of spare rotors, which is nice, however even after using this in a parking lot, I've not yet broken anything. The body of the unit, which offers some protection to the electronics (which then have another plastic dome atop them), comes in several types...bumble bee, UFO, spaceship, etc. Ideally, you might be able to fly w/o it, shaving off some weight and possibly some air resistance, though the fairing does offer some protection and probably shouldn't be removed until you're past the beginner stages.

The battery lasts 8-10 minutes, depending upon how you're flying it. I've found they last more outdoors, probably because you're not making so many direction adjustments. You can get extra batteries and chargers, and I'd recommend it, as 10 minutes isn't enough...you're going to want more. The batteries charge off a USB cable, whether plugged into a computer or using a USB/wall adapter. Charge time is about an hour, give or take.

The directions are just OK, and you'll have to experiment to really get a feel for things. The most important thing to remember is when starting off, you want to try and be on as level a surface as possible, as each time you insert the battery, the thing will auto-level and find it's artificial horizon. If you start off on a slope, you may find the unit won't fly very well, or you'll need to make significant trim adjustments.

The process to start the unit is as follows:

1. Ensure battery for the copter is out, and the remote is off.
2. Insert the battery and immediately place the copter on a flat surface. You should see the slow blinking LED under the fairing
3. Turn the remote on.
4. Move the throttle/rotate lever (on the left of the remote) up once (you'll hear a beep) and then down once (you'll hear a beep).
5. The copter LED should then stop blinking and remain steady RED. You're ready to go...
6. If the copter doesn't start, turn the remote off, then on, and repeat the process w/ the throttle (you shouldn't need to remove the battery). I find I need to do this process twice each time the batter is replaced.

If you crash the copter, you just need to right it, and start flying again...it will automatically reset, and there's nothing you need to do with the remote or unit to get things going again. The only exception to this is if the batter flies out when the crash occurs...then start from step 1 above.

The two things I'd probably change about this unit are to have some LED lights that show the "front" of the copter; as it is, the rotors are white in the front and black in the back...this does help. Secondly, the batter insert/removal is somewhat clunky, but it does work. I'd like to see something a little easier to work with, as getting the batter in and out can be a little difficult sometimes.

So...this is a great copter, and the perfect unit for a child, or an adult (I'm 39) to start off with quad-coptering. Enjoy.

-J
text_fidelity_b: SYMA X1 4 Channel 2.4G RC Quad Copter, Spacecraft (As Shown)

text_fidelity_a:
WB Games Lego Marvel's Avengers - Playstation Vita Compared to other Vita Lego games, it is disappointing. Those who played other games on consoles are probably happy, since it sounds closer to a console in terms of content, but, honestly, it is disappointing, and a bit broken.

First of all, I hate the city hub. It is too big. While it does come into play a bit during the main gameplay, having to navigate it during cleanup is a pain. Trying to find all the collectibles that are scattered throughout the city is annoying, even with a guide. Half of them are in such obscure places that you would never think to look for them there, let alone be able to see them from the distance (if they even render if you just pass by). The missions in the city are just painful; while the smash challenges are easy enough but rely more on luck than anything, the ground and jumping time trials are manageable, but the flying ones are utterly impossible. Precision flying controls with constant change in altitude are ridiculously broken, particularly when you can't see where you are supposed to go. I easily plat any other Vita Lego games, as they are easy and relaxing. And in this game, I have everything else done, but these flying challenges, I just give up on them.

Speaking of the trophies, several of them are glitched; even if you complete everything they still do not show up. And the game is glitched too; I had to restart the game at least twice because it froze and I could not move at all.

The main mission was on the shorter side. Apparently, the console had extra missions about Cap 2 and Thor movies. Rather than having Manhattan hub, I honestly would have preferred a few extra levels. Also, they did have many cutscenes from the movies, but they cut out the punchlines of most of those scenes, which was also pretty disappointing,
text_fidelity_b: WB Games Lego Marvel's Avengers - Playstation Vita

You will need (at minimum) a hammer and a punch (or you can put the geode in an old sock and bash it on the ground).... If you want to make the most of this kit, you will need to get a diamond saw blade and carefully cut them open.

Again, this is an interesting gift for kids. Don't expect too much. It is work to open the geodes (if you want them to look nice) and they are somewhat small in size. However, economically, from a business stand-point.... this is a good value for what they are delivering to you. Weight equals money these days when it comes to shipping.....

text_fidelity_a:
Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb. Most reviews mention the mind-boggling size of the model; I figured that it was because when we gain fatty tissue, it's distributed in a thin layer over our bodies, so seeing it as a lump would be surprising to most people.

     Even with the warnings, I was still shocked! It looked like it had to be 8-10 pounds, not a mere 5! And it FELT like 6-8 pounds...

After a while, I got curious as to why it seemed so disproportionately large. I'm aware that I consistently make terrible (truly awful) estimations of volumes, distances, and weights, so I measured it, just to get the actual numbers.

     My kitchen scale gave the model's mass as 5.293 pounds. That's a forgivable degree of error: 6%. Definitely closer than my awful guesstimate of 6-8 pounds.

     I used displacement to measure the volume as 11.75 cups. [I filled a container to overflowing with water. I added the model to displace some water, then removed the model. I carefully measured how much water I added to completely refill the container.]

     Google conversions gives 11.75 cups as being 169.6 in^3. Various sites list the volume of a pound of adipose tissue as being 29 in^3, 29.5 in^3, 30.08 in^3, and 30.42 in^3.

Using the model's volume and the lowest density, I calculate the model's representative mass as:
169.6 in^3 ÷ 30.42 in^3/lbs = 5.577 lbs

And using the highest density to calculate my model's "mass":
169.6 in^3 ÷ 29 in^3/lbs = 5.8 lbs (17% greater than 5 pounds, but well under my 8-10 pound guess.)

So whether you are measuring by weight or volume, the model is 6-17% oversized. That's far more accurate than seemed possible.

Obviously the manufacturer had to compromise between approximating the coloration, texture, pliablity, volume, and weight. I'm not a surgeon, so I'm clueless as to the accuracy of the coloration, texture, and pliablity. I am disappointed that the volume (which was the characteristic I was most interested in) was off by more than 5%.
text_fidelity_b: Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb.

Little Live Aqua Dragons - Deep Sea Habitat - LED Light Up Tank Hatch and Grow Aquatic Pets | Amazon Exclusive I still have fond memories of Sea Monkeys from when I was a child. It's one of those simple things that bring great joy. As far as I can tell, these are the same thing, only they're called Aqua Dragons. The aquarium is also bigger than the one I had as a child. This set comes with a pouch of eggs, a pouch of food, a spoon, a bubble creator(suction tube), a little magnifying glass, and the aquarium. The aquarium has a removable top and lights that come from the bottom. Simply press a button on the side to turn them on and press it again to turn them off. It comes with batteries, though it does say they're only temporary for the "try me" feature and should be replaced. Non-chlorinated water is recommended.

We've had great fun with our little dragons. It took close to 48 hours for us to be able to see them. Of course, at that point they're only a tiny white dot and it gets more fun when they're bigger. This set has potential to last quite awhile, too. The Aqua Dragons can live up to 6 months. After they all die, you're supposed to completely let the tank dry out. This will cause any eggs to dry out. (Don't wash it out or the eggs will be washed away. The eggs won't hatch unless they've dried out.) Once that happens, you can add more water and start with a fresh batch of little dragons.

It's a great kit to create some special childhood memories.

Note on the aquarium: Don't pull the plastic. I thought it had a protective layer and almost started peeling it off. If you do, the design on it will come off with it. I do wish the plastic was flatter against the aquarium, so it's not as big of an issue thinking it's supposed to be peeled off.

On High mode it really tilts.

Fun
Finding a good building to fly in is key. The building I work in has an open 4 story architecture with bridges at each level. The flip button is also fun for impressing on lookers.

Note
Plug the battery in when it is level so that the gyros are initialized correctly.

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll Since the first Barbie doll was created in 1959, little girl's have always loved to style/color Barbie doll's hair, and this fun to color hair Barbie is no exception. (I took my 1960's ponytail down, so she could look like Sleeping Beauty back in the day!) This gorgeous Color Stylin' Hair Barbie is a huge favorite with the grandchildren now.

Barbie comes with a suction cupped chair, comb, applicator brush, bowl, seven color swatches in 3 colors-3 pink, 2 purple and 2 orange, clip on foiler holder and rubberbands. Barbie is dressed in a glittery pink dress with shoes, necklace and belt. The color application is easy- seat Barbie in her chair, which doesn't move due to an ingenious suction cup bottom, wet the hair section you want to color, place the color swatch in the foiler, then clip the foiler to the wet hair and pull through. When you want to remove the color or color again, you just wash and dry the hair and you are ready for more fun.

There are a couple things you should know before using this coloring set: don't color near carpet, furniture, walls or clothes you don't want to ruin, as these colors can be a permanent stain for certain fabrics or walls. I laid down a cheap plastic tablecloth from the dollar store, so the girls had a great area to play on with no worries. I called Mattel, and found they do not sell extra color swatches, so once these are used up, they are gone, and to replace the colors, you would have to buy another doll. This is a shame, as they always sell accessories and extra hair swatches for the dolls with hair swatches that can be cut, so why not some inexpensive color swatches too Mattel?

The girls just love coloring, braiding and styling the gorgeous streaked areas of this Barbie's hair, so of course they want more colors- and even different colors too. As for something interesting I noticed, I bought another one of these dolls, as I have 2 granddaughters, and we immediately noticed one set colored darkly and another set colored very faintly. I looked closely at the boxes and what did I find on the backs of the boxes, but an expiration date! It says Best Used By and then a date which you need a magnifying glass to read. Reading the back of our boxes showed that one of the boxes colors was expired! That explains the faint color! Being a wonderfully fun to play with Barbie gives this doll 5 Stars, but color that is expired and having no refills brings her down to limited playability with the color, making this gorgeous Barbie a 4 Star doll.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll

PLANET BAKE Vegan Donut Making Kit - Plant-Based, Gluten Free Donut Kit with Pre-Measured Ingredients & Silicone Donut Molds - Complete Kids Baking Set for Ages 4-12 (Vanilla) I also tried the chocolate version of this donut kit and was quite disappointed in the taste of the donuts. This vanilla option is much better. In anticipation of less than ideal taste I added some good quality vanilla extract which also helped boost the flavor.

Still, the issues I had with the chocolate version are also present in this version. The box it comes in is cheap and flimsy, and dented up quite a bit in transit. It makes for a poor presentation should this be a gift item. On the plus side, the sprinkle packet stayed closed in the vanilla kit box (it broke open in the chocolate kit box and there were sprinkles everywhere). The frosting packet is inside the main pouch with loose flour, so it's a messy proposition to get the frosting packet out -- flour spills easily. Lastly, the silicone molds are quite flimsy. Putting them into something supportive, such as a muffin tin, is highly recommended prior to filling and baking.

The vanilla donuts have a much better flavor than the chocolate, especially when additional vanilla extract is added. The assembly process is simple and, while kids will need supervision (especially when dealing with the silicone molds) it's a fun activity.

Taking all the pros and cons into consideration puts my score at 3.5 stars. It's a great idea, but some of the kinks need to be ironed out to make it a kit that is worth the price charged.
text_fidelity_b: PLANET BAKE Vegan Donut Making Kit - Plant-Based, Gluten Free Donut Kit with Pre-Measured Ingredients & Silicone Donut Molds - Complete Kids Baking Set for Ages 4-12 (Vanilla)

text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer Kid & Cargo with Canopy, Folding Wagon with 2 Versatile Seats, (Amazon Exclusive) (3965Z), Red The Canopy and two seats (that can easily be used or not as your needs change) with seatbelts features take this from a standard utility cart to a multi-purpose cart that is good for both transporting stuff and transporting kids. Even when out in the sun. Also the end storage net is very nice because even if the kids take up a big chunk of the available space, you can still store a bag or two or three depending on how well you pack. On the other end the two drink holders mean you don’t have to carry your drinks. Handy if you have kids prone to tossing bottles around as they’ll be within easy reach of you, but not in eyesight of the little ones.

Although it is more useful in that sense than some other carts, it does have some faults. The Velcro that holds the handle against the cart when not in use is almost more trouble than it’s worth. It’s not very sturdy, so if you even lightly bump the handle, it pops the Velcro open and the handle falls. Also the seams at the bottoms are exposed instead of being finished properly, leaving it more open to fraying or damage. The wheels are much larger than most utility carts, so the turning radius isn’t as good as our other carts. Going down a hill, it almost wants to get away from you, though that is an issue with most carts. The canopy is useful but works almost like slap bracelets, so getting it to stay is tricky at first, I’d almost prefer straps that just hold it in place around the retractable poles.

Overall, this is not a perfect cart, but it still very nice despite its faults. The canopy is optional and takes up almost no storage space because the poles are retractable into the cart, so you only need to roll up the fabric and stick in the net storage. The seats are perfect for young kids. It can go back and forth between kiddie wagon and an ideal cart for things like flea markets.

I was torn on the star rating, and rounded up to 4. I’d actually put this at about a 3.5. Do keep in mind that it doesn’t come with any tools, so you’ll need your own (a hammer, a wrench, and a screwdriver).
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Kid & Cargo with Canopy, Folding Wagon with 2 Versatile Seats, (Amazon Exclusive) (3965Z), Red

Folkmanis Grunting Pig Hand Puppet, Standard Packaging, Pink Let’s just say. . . I’m not “squealing with laughter” as it shows on the listing in several places.

First of all. . . This is NOT a pretty pig. It’s kind of “odd” because the color is different in the pictures (the picture of the girl holding it makes it look white with a little tan and black splotches. . . which it is not). The one that I received looks like different shades of tan with some dark splotches. Not the least bit pink. . . not the least bit attractive. I understand that not all pigs are pink in real life. . . and not all pings are “pretty”. . . but when you’re making a toy, then the majority of the time they are pink. . . and they should be at least “not-ugly”, which this one is. . . ugly.

The pictures show the pig standing. This pig does not stand. It lays flat down, with the legs forward. There is nothing stiff in the legs so that it can stand, and it’s obviously made to lay flat.

The “puppet part”. There is a “slit” in the bellow where you put four fingers. You have to find the holes for the fingers for the two front legs. Then you use two fingers to move the mouth up-and-down. Not the easiest thing to do.

The pig “grunts” when you squeeze the “rump” part of the pig. Again, not the best design, in my opinion.

There is a tag that shows that this pig won the 2014 “plush toy” award, which I find very hard to believe.

Finally. . . This is a Made in China toy. . . At the current price it’s WAY too expensive for Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Folkmanis Grunting Pig Hand Puppet, Standard Packaging, Pink

Camera for Kids, 2.7K 48MP Digital Camera for Teen Boy and Girl with 32GB SD Card 16X Zoom, Compact Portable Mini Toys Cameras Christmas Birthday Festival Gift for Kid Children Teen(Pink) I took this out of the box, put in the enclosed micro card and battery (it comes with 2) and then used the cord to charge the camera/battery. I left it charging overnight, so that may be a mistake, but when I went to use the camera it took one picture then shut down. I tried again later and it took 2 pictures then shut down. I have not tried it again since. I am leaving the batteries to fully discharge then I will charge them again and see what happens.
This camera comes with everything you need to begin using it-the micro sd card with an adaptor plus 2 batteries, I appreciate that this is all included especially the adaptor. It has the USB charging cord and a wrist cord which I cannot get to fit into the camera. It also comes with a pouch.
The camera itself is lightweight plastic that feels cheap but at this price point it's probably what you'd expect. I like the color, a very pretty baby pink. The screen is a good size so it will be easy to see.
I can't comment on how it works at this point so I will update after I try it again.
